History:
- Chief complaint: Acute shortness of breath while sitting and watching TV.
- Onset/duration: Began about 1 hour prior to call; new symptom.
- Progression: Not clearly worsening; patient feels stressed and notes heart “really going.”
- Associated symptoms: Nonproductive cough starting yesterday; palpitations; chest soreness with deep inspiration; C-section scar tenderness.
- Denies: Chest pain at rest; sputum production.
- Context: 4 weeks postpartum after C-section; no prior similar episodes. Infant well; no sick contacts reported.

Past Medical History:
- Surgical: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Chronic conditions: None reported.
- Medications: Codeine for post-op pain (dose/route/frequency not documented); used regularly post-op but not taken for approximately 1 week.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction not documented).
- Family history: Mother has had leg clots (patient volunteered).
- Social: At home with infant; partner at work.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth assessment; no vitals documented.
- Patient-reported findings: Shortness of breath at rest; chest soreness on deep breath; tender C-section scar; palpitations.
- Pulse check over phone: Patient counted 30 beats during timed count (duration not specified); clinician assessed heart rate as “slightly fast.”
- No report of chest pain at rest. No sputum production reported. Infant well; no respiratory illness in household noted.

Impression:
- Acute dyspnea 4 weeks postpartum with palpitations and pleuritic chest soreness—concern for pulmonary embolism; differential includes postpartum anxiety and viral respiratory illness.

Management Plan:
- Urgent hospital evaluation advised due to postpartum status and new dyspnea.
- Transport: Option of ambulance discussed; patient elected self-transport to hospital promptly.
- Bring necessary items for infant to hospital.
- Hold codeine for now.
- Counseling: Postpartum patients can develop clots in legs or lungs; hospital will assess and can provide treatment to reduce a clot if present.

Patient Summary:
- 4 weeks postpartum patient with sudden-onset shortness of breath at rest and palpitations, with new cough since yesterday. Given postpartum status and symptoms, PE is a significant concern. Patient will proceed to the hospital now for urgent evaluation.

Key Takeaways:
- Go to the hospital promptly today for assessment of shortness of breath.
- Do not take codeine before evaluation.
- Bring essentials for the baby when you go.

Next Steps:
- Immediate presentation to the nearest hospital/emergency department for evaluation and management.
- Further treatment (e.g., anticoagulation) to be determined by hospital team if a clot is confirmed.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full vital signs; detailed review of systems (fever, leg swelling/pain, hemoptysis, syncope); complete medication list with doses; detailed allergy reaction; smoking status; thromboembolic risk factors (immobility, travel, prior VTE); obstetric history details; breastfeeding status.
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth stated by patient as April 20, 1980; clinician later stated 1983 (conflict noted). Pulse count recorded as 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician described rate as “slightly fast.”
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses and incomplete details; no significant audio issues noted.
